articles.headline: US officials report slight flexibility in Russia and Ukraine peace talks
articles.title: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
articles.summary: Senior officials from Moscow, Kyiv and Washington are meeting in Abu Dhabi for trilateral talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine. According to United States officials, both warring sides are showing private flexibility regarding the postwar control of Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region. However, deep disagreements remain over territorial demands and the future security architecture of Europe.
articles.description: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.

articles.headline: Anthropic plans to raise up to $64bn in New York stock market listing
articles.title: Anthropic heads for lower than expected $1.3 trillion valuation in stock market debut
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic is planning to raise up to $64 billion through an initial public offering on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange. The loss-making firm priced shares between $70 and $78 each, yielding a valuation below prior predictions amid market volatility surrounding artificial intelligence investments. According to analyst Fiona Cincotta from City Index, the move demonstrates continued industry optimism despite wider financial concerns.
articles.description: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78.

articles.headline: Russia, Ukraine and U.S. begin peace talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.title: U.S.-mediated talks on ending war between Russia, Ukraine begin in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Delegations from Russia, Ukraine and the United States commenced two days of discussions focusing on security guarantees in Abu Dhabi on November 10, 2026. Moscow and Kyiv remain deeply divided over territorial demands, military limitations and ceasefires. Russian President Vladimir Putin insists on retaining annexed regions and curbing Ukrainian military expansion, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy demands immediate hostilities cessation and rejects territorial surrenders.
articles.description: The two-day session in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February, will focus on security guarantees

articles.headline: Donald Trump says Iran war is militarily over
articles.title: Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely'
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump declared during a White House briefing that the conflict with Iran is militarily finished, citing positive momentum in negotiations following talks with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdul Rahman Al Thani. Trump stated that further military strikes remain unlikely while a naval blockade maintains regional security, despite domestic political fallout and Republican midterm election pressures.
articles.description: The president says the US is keeping "status quo" with Iran but remains “locked and loaded” should the situation change.

articles.headline: Donald Trump says further military action against Iran is not currently necessary
articles.title: Trump says U.S. military action against Iran not necessary ‘at this point’
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump told reporters in Washington that additional military strikes against Iran do not appear necessary at this time. Speaking on Monday, November 9, 2026, Trump stated that he expects the ongoing conflict to conclude fairly soon. However, he emphasized that the United States military remains fully prepared to respond if circumstances change in the region.
articles.description: “The military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing, but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes,” Trump said

articles.headline: Donald Trump calls Iran war effectively over following discussions with Qatari officials
articles.title: After meeting Qatar PM, Trump calls Iran war ‘effectively over’ militarily
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated that the military conflict with Iran is effectively finished following talks at the White House with Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani. Speaking in Washington, Trump said regional allies prefer maintaining naval blockades. Iranian officials dismissed the remarks as a distraction while expressing openness to further negotiations without coercion.
articles.description: Iranian officials dismissed Trump's remarks as 'fake news' after he suggested keeping the 'status quo'.

articles.headline: Qatar PM meets with Trump for talks on ending war on Iran
articles.title: Qatar PM meets with Trump for talks on ending war on Iran
articles.description: Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani has met with US President Donald Trump.

articles.headline: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese intelligence ties
articles.title: Nvidia shares slump amid investigation into CEO Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia shares dropped more than 4 percent after the semiconductor giant launched an independent board inquiry into Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. The probe examines whether Huang was targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation through a former executive at Megaspeed. Huang stated he will fully cooperate with the investigation while broader technology stocks rose on US markets.
articles.description: Huang admits infidelity, denies compromising Nvidia security as China spy inquiry shakes $4.5 trillion AI firm.

articles.headline: Rubio defends Iran war as necessary protection against nuclear threats
articles.title: Rubio says Trump's war against Iran not 'necessarily popular' but needed to stop a nuclear threat
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the military campaign against Iran on November 7, 2026, stating it was launched to neutralize nuclear dangers despite political fallout. The conflict has impacted the economy and contributed to Republican losses in Congress. Meanwhile, mediators are attempting to revive diplomatic talks as regional tensions remain high and military strikes continue.
articles.description: America's top diplomat offered a robust defence of the more than eight-month-old war even as voters blamed Mr. Trump's policies for the hit to their pocketbooks, including higher energy prices that stemmed from disruptions to shipments in the Strait of Hormuz

articles.headline: Trump announces possible trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin next week
articles.title: Trump says likely to meet Putin, Xi at China APEC summit
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated on November 8, 2026, that he plans to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin during the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Beijing confirmed it is communicating with relevant parties regarding the gathering. The agenda is expected to cover global issues, though analysts note significant political hurdles and differing national priorities among the three nations.
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump indicated to reporters that a deal on the Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran issue and nuclear arms control would be on the agenda

articles.headline: US military member arrested in the UK on suspicion of espionage
articles.title: US soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia
articles.summary: British authorities detained an unidentified 41-year-old United States military member near Gloucester on Tuesday under the National Security Act 2023 for allegedly assisting a foreign intelligence service. London Metropolitan Police counterterrorism forces collaborated with the FBI and US military on the operation. The suspect remains in custody in London while officers search two Gloucestershire properties.
articles.description: London Metropolitan Police says its 'counterterror' forces worked closely with the FBI and US military to make arrest.

articles.headline: Nvidia hires law firm to investigate CEO affair with alleged spy
articles.title: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
articles.summary: Nvidia has appointed New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen and Katz to examine a romantic relationship between Chief Executive Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a Singaporean executive at customer firm Megaspeed whom the US government alleges is a Chinese spy. The independent probe runs alongside an FBI investigation as the company faces scrutiny and falling stock market values.
articles.description: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.

articles.headline: Congressional report finds federal failures in Jeffrey Epstein investigation
articles.title: US federal authorities could have prevented Epstein crimes, report finds
articles.summary: Crimes committed by late financier Jeffrey Epstein after 2005 could have been prevented due to investigative and prosecutorial failures, a congressional investigation concluded on Tuesday. The Republican-led House Oversight Committee released its final report following a fifteen-month review, criticizing the united states attorney office for a 2007 agreement allowing Epstein to evade federal prosecution. The panel also cited institutional failures at the New York prison where Epstein died in 2019.
articles.description: The report by a Republican-led congressional committee follows a 15-month investigation into the handling of the late disgraced financier's case.

articles.headline: Salvadoran troops target Haitian gang in operation leaving 20 dead
articles.title: Salvadoran troops target Haitian gang, leaving 20 dead
articles.summary: Salvadoran forces supported an operation by Haitian police on Sunday that targeted the 400 Mawozo gang headquarters in Croix-des-Bouquets, resulting in twenty deaths. Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele announced the attack on social media platform X. Amnesty International subsequently urged both governments to ensure that all military deployments comply strictly with international human rights law.
articles.description: Salvadoran troops backed the police operation ahead of the Haitian prime minister’s visit to El Salvador.

articles.headline: US administration proposes new eligibility rules to cut food aid
articles.title: Trump administration seeks to cut food aid for more than six million people
articles.summary: The United States Department of Agriculture published a proposed rule on Tuesday to eliminate automatic Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program eligibility tied to Temporary Assistance for Needy Families. The change would remove approximately 6.3 million people from the federal food aid programme and strip 1.8 million children of free school lunches, prompting strong criticism from Democratic lawmakers.
articles.description: Trump’s proposal builds on earlier cuts to federal food aid programme used by more than 36 million low-income Americans.

articles.headline: Republicans elect Jim Jordan as new US House minority leader
articles.title: Republicans elect Trump ally Jim Jordan as new US House minority leader
articles.summary: House Republicans chose Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan as their new minority leader in a secret ballot vote on Tuesday following their midterm election losses. Jordan, who currently chairs the House Oversight Committee and cofounded the House Freedom Caucus, defeated Steve Scalise to succeed Mike Johnson as the top Republican in the chamber.
articles.description: Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan to succeed Mike Johnson as GOP minority leader, promising unity and a robust opposition.

articles.headline: Rubio says no need for major combat operations against Iran
articles.title: Rubio says no need for major combat operations against Iran
articles.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says there is “no need” for further major combat operations against Iran

articles.headline: Protests erupt in Bangladesh demanding return of ousted prime minister
articles.title: Violence erupts in Bangladesh as ousted PM's supporters stage protest
articles.summary: Demonstrations broke out across Bangladesh as supporters of deposed leader Sheikh Hasina demanded her return from exile in India, leading to clashes with security forces and the death of a 60-year-old bus driver in Faridpur on Tuesday. Protesters blocked traffic on the Padma bridge and set fire to police and passenger vehicles. Government officials rejected passport requests and called her a fugitive facing a death sentence.
articles.description: Supporters of Sheikh Hasina want her to return from exile in India.

articles.headline: Nvidia chief executive admits affair with woman suspected of Chinese espionage
articles.title: The US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown it
articles.summary: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang revealed an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence operative, raising concerns among experts that the security breach could destabilize the American artificial intelligence industry and threaten technological advantages. The situation risks disrupting critical chip supplies and compromising strategic insights into White House planning and Silicon Valley infrastructure development.
articles.description: As espionage targets go, Jensen Huang is perhaps one of the least surprising on Earth. The Nvidia CEO runs one of the world's most valuable companies, controls the in-demand technology fueling the AI boom, and is cozy with presidents, CEOs, and all manner of important people. He also wears a cool leather jacket. Which makes […]

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: 14-year-old killed in West Bank raid
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: 14-year-old killed in West Bank raid
articles.description: Israeli forces kill a 14-year-old Palestinian boy in Burqa, as settlers assault a woman near Hebron.

articles.headline: Former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak begins house arrest
articles.title: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
articles.summary: Disgraced former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak arrived at his Kuala Lumpur residence on Tuesday to serve the remainder of a corruption sentence under house arrest. The seventy-three-year-old was escorted by a heavily armed police convoy after a high court ruled the transfer effective immediately following a royal pardon. Najib previously served four years in prison for embezzling funds from the one million development berhad sovereign wealth fund and faces another pending sentence.
articles.description: Najib Razak was convicted for his role in the billion-dollar scandal involving the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund.

articles.headline: Iran remains committed to nuclear non-proliferation treaty
articles.title: Iran backs nuclear treaty even as hardliners raise prospect of bomb
articles.summary: Iran maintains its commitment to the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons despite restricting cooperation with the international atomic energy agency following military attacks, foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei stated on Monday. While hardliners in Tehran discuss potential changes to nuclear doctrine after facility strikes, limited inspections resumed at the Bushehr nuclear power plant. Mediated talks continue between Tehran and Washington to prevent further regional escalation.
articles.description: Iran says it is committed to non-proliferation treaty, but hardliners may be pushing for a change in nuclear policy.

articles.headline: State security forces restrict access to proposed Siang dam site
articles.title: The Siang dam and a threatened homeland
articles.summary: Central security forces and State police have deployed barricades and concertina wires near Parong village in Arunachal Pradesh to restrict unauthorized access to the Siang river. Parong in Siang district is one of three proposed locations identified for a Pre-Feasibility Report regarding the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project developed by the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation.
articles.description: The Adi community has been protesting against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, saying it threatens their land, livelihoods, and civilisation. The agitation has turned violent in response to increasing use of force by the State authorities. The community alleges that the State government has used deceit, force, and threats to get consent for the feasibility study. Abhinay Lakshman reports on the resistance

articles.headline: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion valuation in upcoming stock market debut
articles.title: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion valuation in massive stock market debut
articles.summary: Anthropic launched its investor roadshow on Tuesday seeking a valuation of up to one point four trillion dollars in an upcoming initial public offering to raise sixty-four billion dollars. The creator of the claude artificial intelligence chatbot filed with the securities and exchange commission to offer 825 million shares. Backed by major technology firms including Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, and advanced micro devices, the company reported third-quarter revenues of seventeen billion dollars amid explosive growth.
articles.description: The maker of Claude is looking to raise up to $64.4bn in one of the largest IPOs in history next week.

articles.headline: Israel new parliament sworn in amid government formation efforts
articles.title: Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government
articles.summary: Israel inaugurated its new parliament on Tuesday, setting off a critical political contest as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot attempts to build a coalition to oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. President Isaac Herzog tasked the former army chief with forming a government after securing 67 parliamentary endorsements. Eisenkot must navigate deep divisions over military conscription and relations with Arab-led parties to succeed during his 28-day window.
articles.description: Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has first chance to build a new government and oust the prime minister.

articles.headline: Myanmar military captures 11 resistance bases during southern offensive
articles.title: Myanmar army seizes key resistance headquarters and 10 bases held by opposition, state media says
articles.summary: Myanmar's military seized a resistance command headquarters and 10 other bases in a jungle region near the border between Mon state and the Bago region during a six-day operation, state media reported on November 10, 2026. The captured positions included facilities linked to the National Unity Government and the Karen National Liberation Army, located about 120 kilometers northeast of Yangon.
articles.description: The PDF emerged after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021 and has since formed loose alliances with ethnic militias fighting the military.

articles.headline: Delhi voter deletion applications concentrate on three Muslim neighborhoods
articles.title: Delhi SIR: Why BJP BLAs’ voter deletion applications in Mustafabad focused on three neighbourhoods
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party-appointed booth level agents filed 796 voter deletion applications in Delhi's Mustafabad that were concentrated across 25 polling booths in Nehru Vihar, Dayalpur, and Chandu Nagar. According to an analysis of records and local interviews by The Hindu published on November 10, 2026, all targeted electors were Muslim and selected from areas with sizeable populations and few initial draft roll deletions.
articles.description: 796 Form 7 applications against Muslims, filed by 20 BJP BLAs, concentrated on the rolls of 25 polling booths in Mustafabad. However, BJP claims it has not directed the filing of these applications

articles.headline: Israel's new parliament convenes as Eisenkot seeks to form government
articles.title: New Israeli parliament to take aim at Netanyahu as Eisenkot seeks government
articles.summary: Israel's new parliament convened on November 10, 2026, as political rival Gadi Eisenkot pursued a coalition government within a 28-day window provided by President Isaac Herzog. Eisenkot's bloc aims to target caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and investigate security failures from the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack, though securing a majority requires delicate alliances among fragmented political factions.
articles.description: President Isaac Herzog, ceremonially opening the session, called on all sides to work together and avoid a fresh election in a deeply polarised country weary from three years of war.

articles.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon model with new agent swarm feature
articles.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature
articles.summary: Google is rolling out its Gemini 4 Carbon artificial intelligence model to the general public and paying developers following a limited release to cybersecurity defenders. Billed as the company's strongest model yet for complex reasoning and open-ended research, Carbon is available via the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and a new agent swarm feature on the Antigravity platform.
articles.description: Google is rolling out its latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, to the general public after releasing it to a select group of "cybersecurity defenders" two weeks ago. Google claims Carbon is its "strongest model" yet, and capable of competing with the very best systems from Anthropic and OpenAI. Google says Gemini 4 Carbon "pushes […]

articles.headline: EU climate chief Wopke Hoekstra warns of low COP31 summit expectations
articles.title: EU climate chief Wopke Hoekstra warns 'expectations low' from COP31 summit
articles.summary: European Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra stated on November 10, 2026, that expectations are low for the COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, due to complex geopolitics, oil price shocks, and the absence of U.S. officials. Despite the challenges, the European Union climate chief expressed hope for meaningful progress on establishing clean electrification targets by the conclusion of the UN talks.
articles.description: "If indeed we manage to make electrification the sole focus, or close to the sole focus of the COP, I think we have a chance to deliver on something that is truly meaningful," Wopke Hoekstra said

articles.headline: Israeli attacks in Gaza kill six Palestinians including father and son
articles.title: Father, child among six Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza
articles.summary: Israeli military operations across the Gaza Strip resulted in at least six deaths, according to local health sources. Incidents included an air strike on the Ghubain family home in Gaza City, a strike on a tent in Zeitoun, and gunfire in Khan Younis. Meanwhile, the Government Media Office reported that a recent severe storm flooded 70000 tents and caused millions in damages.
articles.description: Israel has killed more than 1,600 people in Gaza since last year's 'ceasefire', the enclave's Health Ministry says.

articles.headline: 'It's a farce': Hegseth's defiant response to impeachment effort
articles.title: 'It's a farce': Hegseth's defiant response to impeachment effort
articles.description: The BBC’s Gary O’Donoghue breaks down how the US defence secretary defended his record after a Republican congressman launched an attempt to impeach him.

articles.headline: Board of peace calls Israel aid response insufficient after floods
articles.title: Board of Peace says Israel's aid response after Gaza floods 'insufficent'
articles.summary: The board of peace called on Israel to immediately allow essential humanitarian supplies into Gaza after heavy rain and sewage flooding affected tens of thousands of tents. In a rare critique, the United States-backed body stated Israeli restrictions exacerbated humanitarian challenges, while Israel argued Hamas must disarm before reconstruction. The United Nations reported that three children and a woman died on Sunday when an embankment collapsed, leaving roughly 65 percent of displaced residents living in makeshift shelters.
articles.description: The group, formed by Trump, issues rare criticism of Israel, while also blaming Hamas for the suffering of civilians in Gaza.

articles.headline: US and Qatari leaders signal potential diplomatic end to war on Iran
articles.title: ‘Positive momentum’: Is the US war on Iran about to end?
articles.summary: Diplomatic efforts to conclude the United States-Israel war on Iran gained traction as US President Donald Trump and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani discussed peace at the White House. While Trump described the conflict as effectively ending following domestic political pressure, Iranian officials maintained a deterrence posture and demanded conditions such as the removal of naval blockades.
articles.description: Domestic pressures are injecting new life into stalled diplomatic talks, but analysts say peace still hangs by a thread.

articles.headline: India offers to mediate Black Sea food corridors amid ongoing conflict
articles.title: Why is India trying to broker a Russia-Ukraine Black Sea food corridor?
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that India is prepared to help establish Black Sea food corridors following a phone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The initiative coincides with United States-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi and aims to restore grain and oilseed exports that have been severely disrupted by port attacks, which have impacted global food supplies and directly affected Indian imports.
articles.description: India has influence with both sides, but shipping security and Russia’s cooperation remain major obstacles.

articles.headline: US Representative Thomas Massie introduces articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth
articles.title: Hegseth impeachment: What is he accused of, and could he be removed?
articles.summary: United States Representative Thomas Massie filed eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of executing unlawful orders and violating the Constitution through military actions in Iran, Venezuela, and Yemen. While top Democrats backed the resolution, Hegseth dismissed the motion as a farce and maintained that the operations were lawful.
articles.description: Eight articles brought by a Republican lawmaker accuse US Pentagon chief of waging unlawful wars on Iran and Venezuela.

articles.headline: U.S. State Department serves notice to India over Pannun lawsuit
articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. court allows Pannun to serve NSA Doval and former intelligence chief Goyal
articles.summary: The United States Department of State delivered a formal diplomatic note to the Embassy of India in Washington regarding a civil lawsuit filed by Khalistan separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. The note, dated October 20, 2026, stems from an alleged assassination plot for which Indian citizen Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty in a New York court in February 2026. Investigators claim Gupta coordinated the plot with Indian government employee Vikash Yadav.
articles.description: Order issued after U.S. State Department serves notice to officials at Indian Embassy in Washington; MEA rejects charges as ‘frivolous’, calls Pannun’s case ‘fabricated and malicious’

articles.headline: G7 ministers meet in Paris to discuss Ukraine and Iran conflicts
articles.title: G7 Ministers meet on efforts to end Ukraine conflict, halt new Iran war
articles.summary: Foreign ministers from the Group of Seven industrialised nations gathered in Paris on November 9, 2026, for two days of talks. European powers aimed to press U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio for a fair settlement in Russia's war on Ukraine and to deter further military action against Iran. Discussions also addressed a donor conference to repair the Chernobyl reactor dome.
articles.description: Ministers from the leading industrialised nations of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States will be gathering with preoccupations strikingly similar to those of the last such meeting in March

articles.headline: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion valuation in upcoming initial public offering
articles.title: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion IPO
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic confirmed that its upcoming initial public offering could value the company at up to $1.4 trillion with shares priced between $70.00 and $78.00 each. According to media reports, trading could begin on Thursday or Friday, making it one of the most valuable publicly traded corporations despite lowered expectations and debates surrounding artificial intelligence safety.
articles.description: Anthropic confirmed on Tuesday that its IPO could be one of the biggest ever, even while falling short of previous expectations. Its IPO price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share, which would put its valuation as high as $1.4 trillion, according to the The New York Times. The Wall Street Journal […]

articles.headline: Pete Hegseth calls impeachment efforts against him a failure
articles.title: Pentagon chief Hegseth calls moves to impeach him a farce that will fail
articles.summary: United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth dismissed impeachment articles introduced against him by Representative Thomas Massie as a farce during a news conference on November 10, 2026. The Pentagon leader defended military operations conducted during the Iran war, while the Kentucky Republican noted that the House of Representatives would hold a procedural vote regarding the resolution.
articles.description: Pete Hegseth made the comment ‌at a news conference a day after U.S. Representative ‌Thomas Massie, a ‌Kentucky ⁠Republican, introduced eight articles of ⁠impeachment against him

articles.headline: Hegseth promises to defend ‘warriors’ as he faces impeachment
articles.title: Hegseth promises to defend ‘warriors’ as he faces impeachment
articles.description: US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has criticised an attempt by Representative Thomas Massie to impeach him.

articles.headline: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth prepares for first Pentagon briefing amid impeachment threat
articles.title: Pete Hegseth to hold first Pentagon briefing since May amid impeachment threat
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced plans to hold a news conference on November 10, 2026, to address an impeachment resolution filed by Representative Thomas Massie. The congressional move follows criticism over military actions in Iran, Yemen, and Venezuela, though President Donald Trump continues to support the Pentagon chief despite widespread political fallout from the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: The briefing will be Pete Hegseth’s first since May even as the U.S. military has kept up intermittent operations against the Islamic Republic as well as fatal strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in Latin America

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit opens in Antalya amid geopolitical tensions
articles.title: COP31 opens as climate and geopolitical pressures mount
articles.summary: United Nations climate talks began on November 9, 2026, in Antalya, Turkiye, with over 100,000 attendees expected. Negotiators from nearly two hundred countries faced difficult discussions regarding the energy transition and funding for developing nations. Observers noted that geopolitical tensions and financial constraints complicate global cooperation during the two-week conference.
articles.description: More than 100,000 people are expected to attend COP31 in a sprawling expo centre in the Mediterranean seaside city of Antalya over the next two weeks

articles.headline: Google expands tensor processing unit lineup to challenge Nvidia
articles.title: Google launches two AI chips as it seeks to challenge NVIDIA’s dominance
articles.summary: Google introduced two new artificial intelligence chip systems, the TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, aiming to challenge Nvidia corporation in the computing infrastructure sector. The new processors are designed for secure inference and memory-intensive workloads, as the technology giant seeks to attract external customers and expand custom accelerator adoption beyond its own data centres.
articles.description: New systems target secure AI inference and memory-intensive workloads as Google seeks to expand enterprise adoption of its in-house AI processors

articles.headline: Attacks escalate between Saudi-led forces and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis
articles.title: Attacks escalate between Saudi-led forces and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis
articles.description: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted missiles fired by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen as attacks between them escalate.

articles.headline: Bangladesh prosecutor says ousted leader Sheikh Hasina faces execution
articles.title: Bangladesh prosecutor says ex-PM Hasina will be executed if she returns
articles.summary: A Bangladeshi prosecutor stated that ousted leader Sheikh Hasina will face execution upon returning home after missing the deadline to appeal her death sentence. Convicted in absentia for crimes against humanity during the 2024 protest crackdown, the 79-year-old former Prime Minister has vowed to return from India in December despite legal risks. Her planned homecoming creates political challenges for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman as authorities manage diplomatic tensions and domestic security concerns.
articles.description: ‘Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict,’ Md Aminul Islam told reporters, responding to reports she planned to return from self-imposed exile in neighbouring India.

articles.headline: Investigation reveals Israeli soldiers operating as West Bank settlers
articles.title: Israeli soldiers are also settlers in West Bank: Al Jazeera investigation
articles.summary: An investigation by Al Jazeera found that Israeli settlers participating in violent attacks in the occupied West Bank frequently return wearing military uniforms to impose orders on Palestinian victims. According to the report, fourteen of sixty-three Palestinians killed by settlers since October 7, 2023, were shot by individuals serving in the army or wearing military uniforms.
articles.description: Blurred lines between Israeli soldiers and settlers fuel systematic West Bank violence and mass displacement.

articles.headline: United States defense secretary condemns impeachment push as sabotage
articles.title: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth calls US House impeachment effort a ‘farce’
articles.summary: United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defended his military record during a Pentagon news conference, dismissing impeachment resolutions introduced by Representative Thomas Massie as a farce and sabotage. Secretary of State Marco Rubio also defended the actions taken, while lawmakers discussed the potential congressional timeline and the votes required for removal from office.
articles.description: Hegseth condemns impeachment resolution against him as 'sabotage', defending his actions and policy decisions.

articles.headline: Bangladesh prosecutor warns Hasina faces execution if she returns
articles.title: Bangladesh prosecutor warns Hasina faces execution if she returns
articles.description: Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal has said ousted PM Sheikh Hasina will be executed if she returns home.

articles.headline: Malaysian court clears legal hurdles for Najib Razak house arrest
articles.title: Malaysian court clears final hurdle for former PM Najib Razak's transfer to house arrest
articles.summary: A High Court in Malaysia removed all legal obstacles for imprisoned former Prime Minister Najib Razak to serve his graft sentence under house arrest at his Kuala Lumpur home until August 23, 2028. According to his lawyer Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, the ruling follows royal clemency and a political party paying a 50 million ringgit fine. The decision covers only his reduced six-year sentence tied to the 1MDB scandal, while a separate 15-year sentence remains under appeal.
articles.description: Najib has been behind bars since August 2022, when the Kuala Lumpur High Court upheld his graft conviction linked to a multibillion-dollar looting of the state investment fund 1MDB.

articles.headline: Supreme Court highlights vehicular emissions as major Delhi polluter
articles.title: Supreme Court goes beyond Deepavali AQI, flags vehicular emissions polluting Delhi air
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India stressed that vehicular emissions are a primary driver of toxic air pollution in Delhi and the National Capital Region, surpassing festival-related concerns. Led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, the court directed local municipal, police, and state authorities from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, and Rajasthan to submit compliance reports on traffic regulations. The bench emphasized immediate intervention and time-bound action plans to curb worsening air quality across the capital region.
articles.description: The court says Delhi and the NCR bear the ‘cumulative burden of vehicular traffic’ and seeks to know what has been done to regulate in the capital the entry and plying of vehicles from neighbouring States

articles.headline: FBI investigates Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese spy affair
articles.title: Trump says FBI looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with 'Chinese agent'
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced that the FBI is investigating Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang regarding an affair with an alleged Chinese government agent named Alice Huang. Nvidia shares dropped over 4 percent following the revelations, and the company launched an independent inquiry. Meanwhile, China denied any plot to ensnare the executive, dismissing the allegations as unfounded smears.
articles.description: The sudden emergence of Nvidia CEO Huang's infidelity has created concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence

articles.headline: Delhi pollution data vanishes from monitoring stations during Deepavali night
articles.title: At peak of air pollution on Deepavali, data goes missing at several government monitoring stations in Delhi
articles.summary: Air quality data disappeared from multiple government monitoring stations across Delhi during Deepavali night, prompting criticism from analysts who noted the missing figures artificially lowered the Air Quality Index. The accused confessed that marital discord and humiliation prompted the killings, and families plan to conduct joint funeral rites.
articles.description: The latest breakthrough came on Monday (November 9, 2026), with the police recovering two more bodies from Shiradi Ghat, in the Western Ghats of Karnataka.

articles.headline: Millions fill Buenos Aires streets to welcome Pope Leo XIV
articles.title: Millions fill Buenos Aires streets to welcome Pope Leo XIV
articles.description: The Pope celebrated an outdoor Mass in Argentina's capital, the second stop on a 12-day tour of Latin America, just three weeks after having had surgery for lung cancer.

articles.headline: President Donald Trump questions integrity of US midterm elections
articles.title: Trump reverses stance, alleges fraud in recent US midterm elections
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump questioned the integrity of recent midterm elections on Truth Social, reversing his earlier acceptance of Democratic victories and congressional majorities. Trump alleged that pre-election polls were inaccurate and that early voting counts prevented Republican wins, though he provided no evidence of fraud. Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer and various Republican figures responded critically to the president's renewed election denialism statements.
articles.description: Democratic Senate leader Schumer criticises Trump's poll denialism, calling it an avoidable return to baseless claims.

articles.headline: Indian Prime Minister Modi discusses bilateral relations with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy
articles.title: Ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks, Modi speaks to Zelenskyy; Jaishankar speaks to Lavrov
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke on Monday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy regarding the ongoing conflict and bilateral ties between Delhi and Kyiv. During the telephone call, President Zelenskyy shared his perspective on recent developments. Prime Minister Modi reaffirmed India's human-centric approach, emphasized dialogue and diplomacy, and conveyed India's readiness to contribute to a peaceful resolution of the conflict.
articles.description: India is ready to mediate to establish grain safety agreement for “food corridors”, says Ukrainian President Zelenskyy

articles.headline: Man arrested in Chhattisgarh for killing four-year-old to sell organs
articles.title: Man kills 4-year-old to sell his organs after watching video on making money quickly
articles.summary: Basudev Korwa was arrested in Jashpur for allegedly murdering his four-year-old relative to sell his organs after watching an online video. According to Jashpur Senior Superintendent of Police Lal Umed Singh, the agricultural labourer used an artificial intelligence assistant in a chatting app to find methods for making money quickly. Villagers discovered the victim's body after the boy's father filed a missing person complaint.
articles.description: 27-year-old Basudev Korwa from Chhattisgarh is accused of having murdered his cousin’s son and extracting the boy’s organs, which he allegedly kept in a plastic bag

articles.headline: Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta ends operations citing government pressure
articles.title: Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta closes citing gov’t clampdown
articles.summary: Russian investigative outlet Novaya Gazeta ended operations due to state pressure, holding its final editorial meeting on Monday. Labeled a foreign agent last September, the publication struggled after banks halted reader donations. Cofounder Dmitry Muratov criticized the closure in Moscow, while the Kremlin described it as a normal change. United Nations human rights chief Volker Turk called the shutdown a devastating blow to independent media.
articles.description: The paper was one of the few remaining outlets in Russia that criticised Moscow's war on Ukraine.

articles.headline: Krakow shooting suspect dies as Poland mourns six victims
articles.title: Krakow shooting suspect dies as Poland mourns six victims
articles.description: A 24-year-old man who killed six people and wounded 15 in a shooting in Krakow, has died in hospital.

articles.title: Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction

articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump questioned the legitimacy of midterm elections in which Republicans suffered sweeping losses, contradicting earlier remarks that he would accept the outcome. Writing on Truth Social, Trump cited vague claims about voting processes. Democrats secured majorities in both the Senate and the House while state and local officials reported problem-free voting.
articles.description: Trump made the claims, without evidence, on Truth Social on Monday.

articles.headline: French government moves planned minimum wage increase forward to quell protests
articles.title: France accelerates minimum wage hike in bid to quell protest
articles.summary: The French government announced it will move a planned 1.6 percent minimum wage increase forward by a month to December 1, 2026, aiming to quell ongoing protests over the cost of living. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu detailed the hike during a press conference on Monday. The adjustment raises the monthly minimum wage by 24 euros to 1,502 euros, though major labor unions dismissed the measure as insufficient.
articles.description: Unions slam the increase as insufficient, as the government seeks to defuse the unrest ahead of upcoming elections.

articles.headline: Israeli President Isaac Herzog tasks Gadi Eisenkot with forming new government
articles.title: Israeli President picks Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu rival, to try to form government
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government following an inconclusive election. Eisenkot, a 66-year-old former military chief, must navigate complex coalition negotiations within a 28-day window after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in the October 27 vote while remaining the largest bloc in parliament.
articles.description: Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he ‌would have a majority of seats in parliament

articles.headline: Donald Trump calls resumption of war with Iran highly unlikely
articles.title: Trump says resumption of war with Iran 'highly unlikely'
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated that renewed fighting with Iran is highly unlikely as long as peace talks progress. Speaking to CNN, Trump indicated that military actions depend on whether Tehran signs a strong agreement. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi previously suggested that negotiations have paused while assessing the impact of recent United States midterm election results.
articles.description: Iran continues to at least partly block traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which has dented oil supplies out of the Gulf.

articles.headline: At least 34 migrants die after Europe-bound boat sinks off Senegal
articles.title: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
articles.summary: At least thirty-four people died when a wooden migrant boat capsized between Dakar and Saint-Louis while heading toward Spain's Canary Islands, according to the Senegalese Press Agency citing an official source. The interior ministry reported one rescue and ongoing search operations. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye pledged to intensify efforts against smuggling networks amid high youth unemployment.
articles.description: The Atlantic crossing to Spain's Canary Islands remains dangerous for migrants seeking a better life

articles.headline: Houthi authorities report forty-four deaths from airstrikes near Sanaa
articles.title: Houthi rebels say at least 44 killed in airstrike near Yemeni capital
articles.summary: Airstrikes hitting homes in the village of al-Shariya near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, killed forty-four people, mostly women and children, according to Houthi health authorities on November 8, 2026. The attacks wounded forty others, including children and women. Anees al-Asbahi, spokesperson for the Houthi-run Health Ministry, blamed Saudi Arabia for the strikes amid an escalation in the civil war.
articles.description: Al-Asbahi said rescue teams were still searching the area for missing people, raising fears that the death toll could rise.

articles.headline: Border clashes in Ethiopia displace more than fifty thousand people
articles.title: More than 50,000 displaced by deadly Ethiopia border clashes
articles.summary: Fighting rooted in a dispute over land and administrative control between Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional administrations has displaced over fifty thousand people. A government-led assessment and Kenya Red Cross regional head Malik Adan confirmed the rising numbers as refugees crossed into Kenya. The conflict sparked tensions over flag displays in Moyale, leading to urgent humanitarian needs.
articles.description: Families arrive in Kenya with little food or shelter as host communities struggle to cope.

articles.headline: CENTCOM announces Task Force Iron Gate to target Iranian supply networks
articles.title: Trump says Iran is sealed off. But can new US task force stop weapons flow?
articles.summary: United States Central Command announced Task Force Iron Gate to prevent Iran from using land routes and the Caspian Sea to transport advanced weapons. Analysts warn the intelligence unit cannot seal borders without regional cooperation and risks widening the conflict. President Donald Trump claimed the unit and naval blockades had effectively sealed off Iran from the world.
articles.description: Analysts say a small intelligence-focused unit cannot seal Iran’s borders, and others warn it could expand the war.

articles.headline: IRGC strikes three tankers near Hormuz over ‘US links’

articles.headline: London court sentences Russell Brand to prison for sexual offenses
articles.title: UK court hands comedian Russell Brand 10.5 years for rape, sexual assault
articles.summary: London's Southwark Crown Court sentenced British comedian Russell Brand to ten years and six months in prison on November 9, 2026. Judge Joel Bennathan condemned the fifty-one-year-old actor as a sexual predator for attacks against four women between 2004 and 2009. Defense lawyers argued Brand is a changed person, while police confirmed he remains under investigation for other allegations.
articles.description: Brand was convicted last week of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three more between 2004 ​and 2009.

articles.headline: Iran maintains war demands despite United States military pressure and strikes
articles.title: Iran stands by demands to end the war as US ramps up military pressure
articles.summary: Iranian officials reported additional United States strikes on Qeshm island on Monday while insisting that the military pressure will not alter demands to end the conflict. Ahmad Nafisi confirmed the southern island was targeted without infrastructure damage. Meanwhile, Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rejected criticism of Tehran's seven-point peace plan from US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, as mediators continue efforts to prevent escalation.
articles.description: Talks aimed at preventing new major fighting between the US and Iran are ongoing.

articles.headline: Delegations from Ukraine, Russia and United States gather for Abu Dhabi talks
articles.title: ‘No concession’: What to expect from Russia-US-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Representatives from Ukraine, Russia and the United States are convening in Abu Dhabi for trilateral negotiations scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday to address the ongoing war. Analysts remain skeptical about achieving substantial breakthroughs given President Vladimir Putin's firm stance and territorial demands. The discussions involve senior officials including US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Ukrainian negotiator Rustem Umerov, and Russian envoy Vladimir Medinsky.
articles.description: A fourth round of peace talks in 2026 takes place this week, with security guarantees high on the agenda.

articles.headline: Donald Trump meets Qatari Prime Minister as regional conflict continues
articles.title: Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar, no imminent deal seen to end war
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump and Vice President J. D. Vance scheduled talks with Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani in Washington on November 9, 2026, to discuss ending the ongoing conflict with Iran. Despite diplomatic engagements following recent midterm elections, senior officials from the United States and the United Arab Emirates expressed skepticism regarding any imminent comprehensive resolution.
articles.description: Mutual attacks continue, with the U.S. striking Iran's Qeshm island overnight, according to Iranian state media, and Iran attacking tankers in the Gulf and ‌Strait of Hormuz this month while its Yemeni Houthi allies have hit Saudi Arabia

articles.headline: Twenty-one migrants and refugees die attempting to reach Crete
articles.title: At least 21 migrants and refugees die trying to reach Greece’s Crete
articles.summary: At least twenty-one individuals lost their lives attempting to reach the Greek island of Crete in separate maritime incidents. The Greek coastguard reported recovering twelve bodies and rescuing eighteen survivors from a vessel on November 9, 2026, while another operation on November 7 recovered eight bodies and saved twenty-eight people with assistance from European Union border agency Frontex aircraft.
articles.description: Greece's coastguard said more than 100 people rescued in several operations off the southern coast of Crete.

articles.headline: Eisenkot chosen over Netanyahu to form Israel’s next government
articles.title: Eisenkot chosen over Netanyahu to form Israel’s next government
articles.description: Israel's president asked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next gov't over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

articles.title: Russia hits power stations in Ukraine, vessel in Black Sea
articles.description: Russia’s armed forces struck three Ukrainian power substations overnight.

articles.headline: World Meteorological Organization projects 2026 among four warmest years
articles.title: 2026 to be one of four warmest years on record: World Meteorological Organization
articles.summary: The World Meteorological Organization released a report on November 9, 2026, at the COP31 climate meeting in Antalya indicating that 2026 will rank among the four warmest years recorded. Global average temperatures between January and September surpassed pre-industrial levels by 1.47 degrees Celsius, driven by rising greenhouse gas concentrations and an intensifying El Nino weather pattern expected to persist into 2027.
articles.description: The key reason behind the rising global temperatures is that the Earth’s energy imbalance is rising, and the earth system is accumulating heat at an accelerating rate, said WMO

articles.headline: Gaza authorities condemn global inaction after mudslide kills five
articles.title: Gaza authorities slam global ‘inaction’ after mudslide kills five people
articles.summary: Palestinian officials criticized international indifference following a landslide in Deir el-Balah that killed five displaced people and left two missing on November 8, 2026. Heavy winter rains collapsed a sandbank onto tents in the central Gaza Strip, where flooding affected approximately seventy thousand shelters and prompted authorities to blame Israeli restrictions for shortages in rescue equipment and construction materials.
articles.description: Four children and a woman were killed after heavy rain caused a sandbank to collapse on their tent.

articles.headline: Nvidia board investigates CEO Jensen Huang amid US-China espionage allegations
articles.title: Why is Nvidia’s Jensen Huang at the centre of a US-China spy scandal?
articles.summary: Nvidia Corporation is facing an independent board investigation regarding whether its chief executive officer, Jensen Huang, was targeted by Chinese intelligence. The controversy follows reports linking him to a former executive at Megaspeed International. The company stated that national security remains unaffected, though Republican lawmakers have called for congressional testimony.
articles.description: Allegations linking CEO to Chinese intelligence shake markets with chipmaker's shares falling more than 4 percent.

articles.headline: Sand embankment collapse kills four people at central Gaza displaced persons camp
articles.title: Four killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses onto tents, health ministry says
articles.summary: Three children and one woman died when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in central Gaza following heavy rain. Five injured individuals were rescued from the site in Deir al-Balah. The Civil Defence service urged international organizations to provide safer shelters, noting that torrential rain had flooded tens of thousands of tents across the territory.
articles.description: Three children are among those killed in the incident that came a day after heavy rain reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents across Gaza.

articles.title: US deports Lebanese consul-general in Detroit over Hezbollah praise

articles.headline: Israeli president tasks opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming government
articles.title: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
articles.summary: President Isaac Herzog has selected opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to attempt forming a new coalition administration following inconclusive election results in Israel. Eisenkot received sixty-seven recommendations in the Knesset parliament compared to forty-six for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The candidate has twenty-eight days to build a stable government, which aims to resolve political deadlock after neither major bloc secured an outright majority.
articles.description: Neither PM Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor that of his rival secured a majority in last week's election.

articles.headline: Overnight strikes between Russia and Ukraine kill one and damage refinery
articles.title: At least four people killed as Russia and Ukraine trade strikes overnight
articles.summary: At least one woman was killed by falling drone debris after overnight strikes between Russia and Ukraine damaged the Kirishi oil refinery in the Leningrad region on November 9, 2026. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced an emergency mechanism for European Union funds. Meanwhile, Russian forces targeted power substations and a cargo ship, though Moscow's claims of arms shipments remain unverified.
articles.description: Russia's second-largest oil refinery is set on fire by drones while Russian strikes target Ukrainian energy sites.

articles.headline: Delhi chokes after Deepavali as smog pushes air quality into ‘severe’ category
articles.title: Delhi chokes after Deepavali as smog pushes air quality into ‘severe’ category
articles.description: A thick blanket of smog engulfed Delhi after Deepavali celebrations, with air quality deteriorating sharply across the capital. Several monitoring stations recorded severe pollution levels, with AQI crossing 400 in parts of the city. PM2.5 concentrations also surged to hazardous levels, far exceeding World Health Organisation guidelines.

articles.headline: Delhi air quality index slips near severe mark after Deepavali celebrations
articles.title: AQI slips to 'severe' in Delhi; Mumbai, Chennai wake up to smog morning after Deepavali
articles.summary: Delhi experienced severe air pollution on November 9, 2026, as the Air Quality Index reached 404 following Deepavali celebrations despite Supreme Court restrictions on fireworks. The Central Pollution Control Board reported spikes across various northern and western Indian cities. Stage III Graded Response Action Plan measures remain in force across Delhi and adjoining districts to prevent further environmental deterioration.
articles.description: Delhi’s air quality plunged to the edge of the “severe” category on Monday as post-Deepavali pollution surged, with AQI readings above 400 across the capital and smog spreading to Mumbai, Lucknow and other major cities.

articles.headline: China dismisses spy plot claims involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.title: China dismisses a spy plot claim involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as smear campaign
articles.summary: Beijing dismissed allegations on Monday that Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang was ensnared in a Chinese spy plot, calling the claims an unsubstantiated smear campaign. The controversy stems from reports that Huang had an intimate relationship with a business executive who U.S. intelligence allegedly identified as an information gatherer for Beijing. Nvidia announced plans to investigate the matter.
articles.description: The chips company CEO is at the center of a controversy over whether he drove sales of advanced computer chips to China, in spite of U.S. tech restrictions aimed at limiting China’s ability to access these advanced technologies

articles.headline: Qatari Prime Minister to meet US President Donald Trump at White House
articles.title: Qatar PM to meet Trump: What’s the latest on US-Iran negotiations?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump is scheduled to hold closed-door talks with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani at the White House on Monday. The discussions occur amid ongoing diplomatic efforts involving Qatari mediation to address differences regarding Iran's nuclear programme, regional security, and terms for ending the current conflict in the Middle East.
articles.description: Iran has put forward a two-day proposal developed with Qatari mediators that Washington is examining.

articles.headline: Delhi air pollution exceeds fifty times WHO limits following Deepavali celebrations
articles.title: Air pollution over 66 times WHO limit in parts of Delhi as people defy ban on firecrackers on Deepavali
articles.summary: Air pollution levels surged past fifty times World Health Organisation limits across areas of Delhi after residents ignored curfews on Deepavali night. Data from the Delhi Pollution Control Committee recorded PM2.5 concentrations reaching 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter in Akshardham and 767 micrograms per cubic meter in Anand Vihar on November 8, 2026, contributing to severe public health risks.

articles.title: Supreme Court terms vehicular emissions major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stated on November 6, 2026, that vehicular emissions heavily drive air pollution in the Delhi-National Capital Region as the air quality index approached the severe category at 391. Speaking at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Guterres urged leaders to accelerate emission cuts. A World Meteorological Organization report confirmed that 2026 continues a streak of exceptional global temperatures and rising sea levels.
articles.description: The UN chief statement came as the UN’s World Meteorological Organization released a report indicating that 2026 has continued a streak of exceptional global temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels

articles.headline: US poll shows majority of voters want Democrats to end Iran war
articles.title: US voters want Democrats focused on ending Iran war, lowering costs: Poll
articles.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll published on Tuesday revealed that seventy-one percent of Americans want congressional Democrats to pass legislation ending the war with Iran, while sixty-two percent support repealing tariffs enacted by President Donald Trump. Nine in ten respondents emphasized that addressing the cost of living should be the top priority during the first hundred days of the new term.
articles.description: Poll shows majority of Americans want Congress to prioritise addressing rising cost of living and economic challenges.

articles.headline: Nvidia investigates reports that CEO Jensen Huang faced Chinese intelligence targeting
articles.title: Nvidia investigating reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence
articles.summary: Nvidia announced an investigation on November 8, 2026, into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence. Huang acknowledged an intimate relationship with a business executive whom United States intelligence linked to Beijing. articles.description: The announcement came after Jensen Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing

articles.headline: Global greenhouse gas emissions reach 54 billion tonnes in 2025
articles.title: Which countries and industries emit the most greenhouse gases?
articles.summary: Global greenhouse gas emissions reached 54.1 billion tonnes in 2025, driven largely by the power sector and industrial manufacturing, according to data from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre and the International Energy Agency. China, the United States, and India remained the world's largest emitters, accounting for nearly half of the total emissions while extreme weather events caused widespread destruction globally.
articles.description: The US has emitted the most CO2 in history; China is now the biggest emitter. Here’s who is driving global emissions.

articles.headline: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requests new passport to return to Bangladesh
articles.title: Ousted PM Sheikh Hasina seeks passport in sign of Bangladesh return plan
articles.summary: Bangladesh ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally requested a new passport and identity card to facilitate her return from India, where she has lived in self-imposed exile for two years. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia last November for her role in a deadly crackdown on student protests in 2024. Her planned return raises potential legal and political complications for the current government.
articles.description: Hasina, who has been living in India for two years, has promised to return to Bangladesh in December.

articles.headline: US Senate advances bipartisan bill to accelerate energy infrastructure projects
articles.title: US Senate advances major bill boosting energy infrastructure
articles.summary: The United States Senate voted seventy-three to twenty-five on Monday to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which aims to overhaul permitting processes for energy projects and require data centres to cover power costs. Supported by President Donald Trump, the legislation promises billions in residential electricity savings while drawing strong opposition from environmental groups and incoming Democratic leaders.
articles.description: Rare bipartisan bill requires data centres to pay for infrastructure, but environmental groups say it falls short.

articles.headline: International maritime body records twenty-five seafarer deaths amid Strait of Hormuz conflict
articles.title: Who are the seafarers caught in the US-Israeli war on Iran?
articles.summary: Commercial vessels navigating through the Strait of Hormuz face severe security threats following nine months of conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran. The International Maritime Organization has documented at least twenty-five deaths among civilian merchant crews, with Indian nationals suffering particularly heavy casualties. Industry groups continue to urge enhanced risk assessments and strict adherence to maritime security guidelines across the volatile shipping corridor.
articles.description: International Maritime Organization records at least 25 deaths since the conflict started on February 28.

articles.headline: Negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and US meet in Abu Dhabi for peace talks
articles.title: What to know about upcoming peace talks involving Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. officials
articles.summary: Negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the United States are scheduled to hold a two-day session starting Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, focusing primarily on security guarantees. The discussions follow previous failed negotiations and a localized truce in Oleshky. Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy remain deeply divided over territorial control and military limitations.
articles.description: The upcoming Abu Dhabi talks focus on security guarantees amid stalled peace efforts and ongoing fighting

articles.headline: FDA orders GLP-1 weight-loss drug makers to add rare eye warnings
articles.title: Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
articles.summary: The United States Food and Drug Administration ordered manufacturers of weight-loss drugs including Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound to include warnings about nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, a rare condition that can cause permanent blindness. While the agency concluded there is an increased risk, manufacturers such as Novo Nordisk stated the data do not definitively establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship.
articles.description: The US Food and Drug Administration says Ozempic, Wegovy, and other weight-loss drugs must have labels about the condition, known as NAION.

articles.headline: British author David Walliams faces accusations of grooming and sexual assault
articles.title: UK children’s author David Walliams accused of grooming minors
articles.summary: Multiple women accuse British author and comedian David Walliams of grooming and sexual misconduct in a joint investigation published by The Guardian newspaper and ITV News on Tuesday. Walliams denies the allegations through his legal representatives while acknowledging thoughtless behavior. Meanwhile, the BBC announced it is reviewing and removing his content from platforms following the publication.
articles.description: A joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News details allegations made by multiple women against the 55-year-old.

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone unit defends Slovyansk amid ongoing bombardment
articles.title: Meet the Peaky Blinders, Ukraine's drone unit protecting a devastated front-line city
articles.summary: Members of a Ukrainian drone unit named Peaky Blinders are intercepting Russian drones in Slovyansk, one of four front-line cities forming a heavily reinforced defense belt in Donetsk. articles.description: Slovyansk continues to be bombarded by Russian forces, making it almost uninhabitable with less than 10% of it's pre-war population remaining.

articles.headline: United States boycotts United Nations human rights review in Geneva
articles.title: Trump administration again boycotts UN human rights review
articles.summary: United States representatives skipped a United Nations examination of the American human rights record in Geneva, prompting the UN body to delay the review until January. The boycott, marking the second consecutive year Washington missed the evaluation, drew criticism from rights groups and experts who warned the absence damages the credibility of the council.
articles.description: UN Human Rights Council delays US human rights record examination until January after Washington refuses meeting.

articles.headline: Hyderabad records hazardous air quality levels following Deepavali festivities
articles.title: Air of Deepavali celebrations lingers in Hyderabad with AQI remaining at hazardous levels
articles.summary: Hyderabad woke up to heavy smog on November 9, 2026, after Deepavali celebrations continued until early morning hours across central localities. Officials from the Telangana Pollution Control Board were reportedly out of order as pollution levels escalated.
articles.description: The air quality in Hyderabad deteriorated in the night itself with particulate matter 2.5 reaching 392 micrograms per cubic meter (μg/m³) at 9.30 p.m. and the Air Quality Index averaged 509

articles.headline: Citizens collective alleges millions of missing voters in Tamil Nadu
articles.title: Over 74 lakh voters missing from Tamil Nadu electoral rolls, says citizens’ collective
articles.summary: The Independent Young Citizens Collective alleged that over seventy-four lakh voters were removed from Tamil Nadu electoral rolls during a revision exercise. Activists demanded an inquiry, the scrapping of the exercise, and the restoration of eligible voters ahead of upcoming elections, while criticizing the heavy administrative burden placed on citizens.
articles.description: The collective has announced a rally on Anna Salai on November 26, as part of a nationwide day of action against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls

articles.headline: Spain faces nationwide strike amid housing crisis and snap elections
articles.title: Spain braces for nationwide strike as anger over housing, costs boils over
articles.summary: Spain is bracing for a nationwide twenty-four-hour general strike called by major unions over soaring rents and living costs, disrupting transport and public services weeks before snap elections. The protest follows widespread anger over housing shortages and evictions, keeping the issue at the center of political debate as political parties clash over responsibility.
articles.description: The 24-hour walkout, called by Spain’s two biggest unions, is due to start on Wednesday.

articles.headline: UK court overturns colonial-era laws criminalising same-sex intimacy
articles.title: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
articles.summary: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London overturned laws criminalising same-sex intimacy in Trinidad and Tobago following an eleven-year legal battle brought by Jason Jones. The historic unanimous ruling determined the legislation violated individual privacy rights, ending laws that had carried harsh penalties based on colonial-era British statutes.
articles.description: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.

articles.headline: French police target drug gangs recruiting children in Marseille
articles.title: Inside the French drug gangs recruiting children to kill
articles.summary: French authorities report that criminal networks, notably the DZ Mafia gang founded by Mehdi Laribi, are increasingly recruiting minors for drug distribution, kidnappings, and murders. Amid soaring cocaine consumption and billions in illicit drug revenue, the exploitation of vulnerable youths persists despite intensive police efforts and recent high-profile arrests across the port city of Marseille.
articles.description: The BBC enters Marseille's dangerous underworld, where young people are trapped, brutalised and exploited.

articles.headline: OpenAI introduces verified business agents for ChatGPT in the US
articles.title: ChatGPT is getting verified AI ‘Business Agents’
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm OpenAI launched verified business agents in ChatGPT to help users with comparison shopping and brand inquiries.
